name: Jack Link
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Jack Link's eponymous meat products company sells 800 million packages of beef jerky, turkey jerky, meat sticks and other goods each year.

Link's great-grandfather emigrated from Germany to Wisconsin in the 1880s, bringing with him his old-world recipes for sausages and smoked meats. His grandfather was butcher and his father raised cattle.
In 1985, with the Link family's meatpacking business bankrupt, Jack Link was inspired to start producing jerky using his great-grandfather's 1880s recipes.
Now Jack Link's is the top-selling jerky brand in America, with $2 billion in estimated annual revenue and 34% of the market.
Jack Link became chairman in 2013 and his son Troy moved into the role of CEO.
The Link family also owns a car dealership, an RV dealership, and ranch and farmland in Minong, Wisconsin, where the company is headquartered.
forbes_facts: Jack Link's beef sticks and jerkies are sold across more than 200,000 stores at nearly every major retailer in America, as well as in 55 countries around the world.

name: Jack Gance
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Jack Gance started the Chemist Warehouse pharmacy chain with Mario Verrocchi in 1995 with five pharmacies.
Today it has annual revenue of A$3.3 billion and over 600 outlets across Australia, China, Dubai, Ireland and New Zealand.
Chemist Warehouse dropped its IPO plan opting for a merger with ASX-listed Sigma Healthcare, which was completed in February 2025.
Gance started his first pharmacy business in 1972 with his younger brother Sam Gance.
forbes_facts: In 1976, Jack and Sam established a successful sunglasses, perfume and suntan lotion company-Le Specs and Le Tan-which they sold in 1991.

name: Jay Paul
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Silicon Valley real estate developer Jay Paul builds and leases office space to big tech firms, including Hewlett-Packard, Amazon and Apple.
His privately held Jay Paul Co. has developed more than 14 million square feet of office space in California and Texas.
His first project in San Francisco-proper was 181 Fremont, a 70-story tower with offices and 67 luxury condos up top, which opened in 2018.
Paul is developing about 4 million square feet of office space in downtown San Jose, with plans for a new office campus and several high-rises.
He also owns properties in Santa Cruz, San Diego and Austin, Texas.
forbes_facts: Paul lives in San Francisco's affluent Pacific Heights neighborhood. He owns two yachts and at least one Picasso painting.
Google leases more than a million square feet of office space from Jay Paul Co.

name: Barry Sternlicht
sec_insider_companies: Starwood Real Estate Income Trust, Inc. (N/A) - Director; ESTEE LAUDER COMPANIES INC (EL) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Barry Sternlicht runs Starwood Capital Group, a private equity firm that specializes in real estate investments.
Starwood Capital has $125 billion of gross assets under management, making it one of the world's biggest real estate investors.
Sternlicht founded Starwood Capital in 1991 and later started the W hotel chain and Starwood Property Trust, one of the biggest mortgage REITs.
Sternlicht has sponsored five SPACs since 2020, including one that took senior care provider Cano Health public in June 2021.
In 2025, Starwood received approval to open an office in Dubai as it plans to invest across the Gulf.
forbes_facts: Sternlicht moved his Starwood Capital Group from its long-time home in Greenwich, Connecticut to Miami, Florida in 2018.

name: Albert Chao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Albert Chao is estimated to own nearly 25% of Westlake Corporation, one of North America's largest producers of low-density polyethylene, used for food packaging and more.
His father T.T. Chao moved the family from Taiwan to the U.S. and founded Westlake in 1986. Albert and brother James Chao are credited with helping launch the company.
Albert was CEO from 2004 to July 2024, when he became executive chairman. James was chairman from 2004 to July 2024, when he became senior chairman.
James and sister Dorothy Chao Jenkins are also estimated to own nearly 25% of Westlake apiece.
Dorothy is married to Charles H. Jenkins, Jr., the former chairman of his family's supermarket chain, Publix. She retired as a director of Westlake in 2023.
Albert's daughter Carolyn Chao Sabat and son John Chao sit on Westlake's board alongside James' daughter Catherine Chao and son David Chao.

name: Bruce Karsh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Bruce Karsh runs Los Angeles-based private equity firm Oaktree Capital Management with longtime partner Howard Marks; they founded it in 1995.
In 2019, Brookfield Asset Management acquired 61% of Oaktree for $4.9 billion in cash and stock. It agreed to buy the rest for $3 billion in 2025.
Karsh still runs the company, which had gone public in 2012 and which continues to operate independently, as co-chairman and CIO.
A leading debt investor, Oaktree manages over $220 billion in assets, two thirds of which is invested in corporate or distressed debt.
forbes_facts: Karsh, a rock-and-roll memorabilia collector, owns the rights to the Beatles' movie "A Hard Day's Night," and co-owns the rights to "Help!"
Karsh is a minority owner of the Golden State Warriors. He made a play for the Los Angeles Clippers in 2014, but was outbid by Microsoft billionaire Steve Ballmer.

name: Alex Beard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Alex Beard retired as head of worldwide oil operations at commodities trader and mining giant Glencore in 2019.
Beard, who had worked at Glencore since 1995, is based in London and was the highest-ranking Glencore executive in the UK.
Before he left, Beard owned a 2.5% stake in the firm, which has assets in oil, gas, agriculture and mining globally.
Prior to joining Glencore, Beard spent five years as an oil trader at BP.
His new investment fund, Adaptogen Capital, is focused on renewable energy opportunities.
forbes_facts: Beard serves on the board of trustees of Shakespeare's Globe, which operates the iconic Globe Theatre in London.

name: Fan Xiulian
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2012-2026)
forbes_bio: Fan Xiulian is the CEO of Haisco Pharmaceutical Group.
The company is known for a range of specialty pharmaceuticals, including those for anesthesia, oncology antiemetics, digestive care, antibiotics, and cardiovascular treatments.
With billionaire Wang Junmin and Zheng Wei, an entrepreneur, the trio acquired the predecessor of Haisco in 2007 and took the company public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2012.

name: Ana Lucia de Mattos Barretto Villela
name_chinese: 安娜·卢西亚·德·马托斯·巴雷托·维拉
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Ana Lucia de Mattos Barretto Villela is a member of one of Brazil's oldest banking families.
Her great-grandfather founded the bank Itau, which merged with Unibanco in 2008 to form Itau-Unibanco, Latin America's biggest private sector bank.
She is one of the largest individual shareholders of Itausa, the bank's holding company, and is vice chairwoman of their board of directors.
Her grandfather founded Duratex, a publicly-traded Brazilian maker of wood paneling and bathroom fixtures; she is a shareholder.
She became a shareholder of the bank when she was 8 years old as her parents died in a plane crash in 1982.
forbes_facts: Villela was named the first female board member of Itau Unibanco, Latin America's largest bank by market value, when she was 44.
She and her husband co-founded the nonprofit Alana, which focuses on promoting the welfare of children.

name: Heikki Herlin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Heikki Herlin, born 1990, is an heir to the Kone fortune in Finland.
He is the great-great-grandson of Harald Herlin, who invested in Kone Elevators in 1924.
Heikki Herlin inherited shares in several Scandinavian companies from his father Niklas, who died in 2016.
His most valuable holdings are stakes in Kone and Cargotec, a producer of machinery for heavy duty cargo ships.
His two uncles and aunt, Ilkka, Antti and Iona Herlin, are all billionaires.
forbes_facts: Like his father, Herlin is a journalist and writer. In 2020, he published a memoir about his father's life.
He is the second largest shareholder of Finnish publishing company Alma Media.

name: George Yancopoulos
sec_insider_companies: REGENERON PHARMACEUTICALS, INC. (REGN) - Bd. Co-Chair, President & CSO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: George Yancopoulos is the chief scientific officer of biotech firm Regeneron.
He received his M.D. and Ph.D. from Columbia University and became a professor of biology by age 28.
Regeneron was cofounded by now-billionaire Leonard Schleifer in 1988. Yancopoulos joined the next year.
Yancopoulos led the invention of eleven FDA-approved drugs and a technology platform designed to invent more.
Yancopoulos owns about 1% of Regeneron stock.
forbes_facts: Yancopoulos was a finalist in the Westinghouse Science Talent Search in 1976. Today, it is called the Regeneron Science Talent Search and sponsored by his company.

name: Richard Barton
sec_insider_companies: ZILLOW GROUP, INC. (Z AND ZG) - Co-Executive Chairman; NETFLIX INC (NFLX) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Richard Barton is the cofounder and co-executive chairman of Zillow Group, an online real estate marketplace.
He and Lloyd Frink launched the business in 2004; Zillow went public seven years later.
Barton served as Zillow's CEO from inception until 2010 and again from 2019 until 2024.
A serial entrepreneur, Barton founded travel booking site Expedia inside Microsoft in 1994 and also cofounded company review site Glassdoor in 2007.
Barton served as a partner at Silicon Valley venture capital firm Benchmark from 2005 to 2018. He also sits on the boards of Netflix and QVC Group.
forbes_facts: Prior to founding Zillow, Barton spent a year living in Italy.
